mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by at least 0.25 percentage points for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises by at least 0.25% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) when GDPC1 YoY change drops below -2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 5% for four consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which raises wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when UNRATE remains below 5% for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a statistical artifact or data inconsistency rather than genuine labor market strength, which historically coincides with short-term S&P 500 volatility and negative 5-day returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE increases in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) when PAYEMS and UNRATE both rise in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for six consecutive months indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate revenue prospects and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) when INDPRO declines for six consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and real housing starts (HOUST) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a broad-based demand recovery, which boosts earnings expectations and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both exceed 12-month moving average in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) when GDPC1 and HOUST both exceed their 12-month moving averages in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate held constant at or below 0.5% for more than six months in a low-inflation environment signals an extended accommodative monetary policy stance, which supports equity valuations and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS <= 0.5% for at least six consecutive months and CPIAUCSL YoY < 2%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) when FEDFUNDS remains at or below 0.5% for six months and inflation is below 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the producer price index for finished goods (not available; using CPIAUCSL as proxy) above 3% for four consecutive months signals rising input costs, which erode profit margins and drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL YoY change > 3% for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) when CPIAUCSL YoY change exceeds 3% for four consecutive months.
